old_caption: The video captures a serene scene in a clear, shallow body of water. Various aquatic plants with green leaves and stems are scattered throughout. Several fish, including dark blue and orange ones, swim among the plants. The camera moves slowly, revealing more of the underwater landscape. Sunlight filters through, casting dappled light on the plants and fish, enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. The overall ambiance is peaceful, with the natural beauty of the underwater environment being the focal point.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene underwater scene in a clear, shallow body of water. The water is filled with various aquatic plants, including green leaves and stems, which are scattered throughout the frame. Several fish, ranging in color from dark blue to orange, swim gracefully among the plants. The fish move fluidly, creating gentle ripples on the surface of the water. The camera pans slowly across the scene, revealing more of the underwater landscape. The sunlight filters through the water, casting a dappled light effect on the plants and fish, enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. The overall ambiance is peaceful, with the natural beauty of the underwater environment being the focal point.
caption: The video captures a shallow, clear pond seen from above, where thin green stems topped with yellow and pale leaves rise from a sandy bottom. Pale reflections of tree trunks and a standing figure stretch across the upper water surface. Two elongated purple fish hover near the center, moving slowly among the submerged stems. A pale fish and a dark fish drift near the upper right, while an orange-and-white fish drifts near the top center. The handheld viewpoint drifts slowly, sliding the plant clusters, reflections and fish toward the right edge and revealing more floating leaves along the left. Light ripples shift subtly from frame to frame, occasionally blurring the scene. The fish keep moving at a slow pace as the clip continues.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside

A pale fish and a dark fish rest near the upper right, while an orange-and-white fish drifts near the top center. review_issues.quote: gradually gliding to the right through the submerged stems
review_issues.problem: The rightward displacement of the two purple fish tracks the same rate as the plant clusters and reflections, i.e. it is produced by the handheld pan; measured against the stems they do not glide right (they roughly hold position or even lag), so this attributes viewpoint motion to the fish's own swimming.

review_issues.quote: A pale fish and a dark fish rest near the upper right
review_issues.problem: These fish are carried toward the right edge by the pan and show their own slow relative drift across the frames, so describing them as 'rest' misstates their visible motion.

review_issues.quote: The fish keep moving at a slow, steady pace as the clip continues.
review_issues.problem: 'Steady' is unsupported: the fish's apparent speed and the scene sharpness fluctuate (several frames are motion-blurred), so the pace is not visibly steady.
